briefing.historical: On 19 November 1942 the Red Army launched Operation Uranus against the Romanian armies guarding the flanks of the German 6th Army at Stalingrad. The Southwestern, Don and Stalingrad Fronts closed the ring around the city on 23 November; Hitler ordered the pocket held and supplied by air, the Luftwaffe delivered less than 20 percent of the 680 tonnes a day required, and Manstein's Winter Storm relief attempt of 12-23 December failed (E01, E03).
briefing.situation: The Soviets must close and hold the ring, defeat the Romanian armies and stop the German relief. The Germans must hold Stalingrad and the airfields, keep the supply line open and relieve the pocket; their fuel and air supply are scarce. Start positions are approximate sector anchors; Italian 8th Army corps and divisions are not included (not retrieved).

playableNations.summary: Three fronts: encircle the 6th Army and stop the relief.
Hold the pocket and break the ring with scarce fuel and a failing airlift.

units.name: Italian 8th Army (army-level element only; corps/divisions not retrieved)

objectives.title: Close the ring at Kalach
objectives.description: Capture Kalach-na-Donu; the 26th and 4th Tank Corps linked up at Sovetsky on 23 Nov (E01).

objectives.title: Push the outer ring: Surovikino
objectives.description: Take Surovikino on the Chir railway.

objectives.title: Break the Romanian Third Army: Kletskaya
Take the airlift base: Tatsinskaya
objectives.description: Capture Tatsinskaya airfield (lost to a Soviet raid, E03).

objectives.title: Take Morozovsk
objectives.description: Capture Morozovsk, the German rail railhead for the relief force (E03).

objectives.title: Stop the relief short of the city
objectives.description: Hold Beketovka until 24 Dec, when Winter Storm collapsed (E03). Beketovka position is approximate.

objectives.title: Stretch goal: Stalingrad
objectives.description: Clear the city (the 6th Army surrendered 2 Feb 1943, E02; beyond this scenario window).

objectives.title: Hold Stalingrad
objectives.description: Keep the city (E01: Hitler ordered an all-round defence, "Fortress Stalingrad").

objectives.title: Keep the Gumrak airfield
objectives.description: Keep the airlift landing ground at Gumrak.

objectives.title: Relief breakthrough: Beketovka
objectives.description: Capture Beketovka south of the city, linking the relief force with the 6th Army (Winter Storm, E03).

objectives.title: Hold Kotelnikovo
objectives.description: Hold the relief force base area.

objectives.title: Break the Don Front north of the city: Kotluban
objectives.description: Capture Kotluban, Soviet-held at the start.

objectives.title: Hold Surovikino
objectives.description: Keep the outer ring from closing on the Chir railway.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, "Operation Uranus" (D-Day 19 Nov 1942 timeline to 24 Nov, strengths, encirclement; text covers little of December; internal conflict on the link-up date 22 vs 23 Nov).
Wikipedia, "Battle of Stalingrad" (timeline, infobox strengths ambiguous; army-level fronts and Axis armies; winter conditions "tens of degrees below freezing").

Wikipedia, "Operation Winter Storm" (12-23 Dec 1942; Little Saturn from 16 Dec; 2nd Guards Army transfer authorised 13 Dec, ready 15 Dec; airlift requirement 680 t/day, under 20% delivered; Tatsinskaya airfield lost to a raid, date not stated in the text read).

Wikipedia, "Operation Uranus Soviet order of battle" (Soviet units as of 19 Nov 1942, north to south: Southwestern, Don and Stalingrad Fronts; armies, corps, divisions, brigades, commanders; cites Glantz 2014; page flags a "two field armies" text/list mismatch, several unlinked entries and an empty Footnotes section).

Wikipedia, "Axis order of battle at the Battle of Stalingrad" (6th Army corps/divisions with commanders; Romanian Third and Fourth Armies; 4th Panzer Army corps). The page spans Sep 1942-Feb 1943 with no single November snapshot, so presence on 19 Nov of each listed division is NOT confirmed by it; Italian 8th Army and Fliegerkorps VIII are not covered.

Wikipedia, Pitomnik Airfield (coordinates 48.7425N 44.25E via the Wikipedia coordinates API). Position only; no tonnage or garrison facts used.

GAME-SCALE ABSTRACTION (internal): manpower, equipment, morale/experience, resources, objective points and thresholds are nominal game values, not historical strengths. German fuel/supply pool scaled to 50% to reflect the sourced airlift shortfall (E03: under 20% of the daily requirement delivered in early December); Romanian and Soviet-reserve quality values are game-scale (E01 states the bombardment targeted non-German units and the Romanian 3rd Army routed).
Position/coordinate policy (internal): place coordinates come from E07/E08 where listed; other unit positions are approximate sector anchors.

POSITION POLICY (internal): no source gives start coordinates for divisions. Positions are approximate sector anchors inferred from named places in E01/E02/E05 (e.g. 62nd Army in Stalingrad on the Volga bank; Serafimovich and Kletskaya bridgeheads on the Don; Stalingrad Front south of the city) with a small deterministic spread; positions are flagged approximate.

BORDER POLICY (internal): initialControl is a coarse snapshot of 19 Nov 1942: Germans/allies west and south of the Don and in the Stalingrad pocket area, Soviets north of the Don bridgeheads and east of the Volga; no front-line detail.
